claims.claim: On September 28, 2026, Cerebras Systems and cloud infrastructure startup Gimlet Labs announced a strategic partnership to deliver ultrafast AI inference.
claims.notes: Verified primary press release issued September 28, 2026.

claims.claim: The partnership targets inference speeds of up to 3,000 tokens per second for real-time agentic and conversational AI workloads.
claims.notes: Targeted specifically at latency-sensitive voice, video, and agentic workflows.

claims.claim: Gimlet Cloud is integrating Cerebras CS-4 systems powered by dinner-plate-sized Wafer Scale Engine processors.
claims.notes: CS-4 systems provide massive on-chip SRAM memory bandwidth.

claims.claim: Gimlet Labs utilizes a disaggregated inference architecture separating the prefill stage on GPUs from the high-throughput decode phase on Cerebras wafer-scale chips.
claims.notes: Optimizes hardware allocation across inference phases.

claims.claim: Cerebras plans to deploy up to 100 megawatts of compute capacity with Gimlet Labs, with the first datacenter operational in late 2026 and broad availability in 2027.

editorial_cautions: Clarify that 3,000 tokens/sec is the target for high-throughput decode on wafer-scale chips in a disaggregated setup.
Mention that first datacenter goes live in late 2026, with broader platform access in 2027.
